attributes.provenance: READ-ONLY investigation by the PAD-SPLIT lane (work_claim.player-pads-2.20260831.v1, worktree GDL-Claude-PlayerPads2, branch claude/player-pads2-20260831), resolving the hypothesis flagged but explicitly not adopted by claim.select-options-pad-run-shopping-list.20260831.v1. Method: exhaustive scan of every src/game/**/*.c file for integer literals in [0x1ECC, 0x3300) used as a pointer displacement off a player base (build/scratch/scan_shadow.py, 3 hits total), plus a name-level grep for every field the header declares in the range, plus reading the two wholesale copy sites and the memset. NO header change was made in this range this run -- that is an integrator decision.
attributes.scope: include/game/player.h, Player range [0x1ECC, 0x3300) and specifically the fields currently declared at 0x2220 (crystals[8]), 0x2230 (gargoyle_items[3]), 0x2236 (legend_items[2]) and 0x224C (field_224C). GC target asm and GC source consumers are the authority; Xbox PDB is reference only.

subject: tu:game/game/player
value: RESOLVED, AFFIRMATIVE, AND STRONGER THAN THE HYPOTHESIS ANTICIPATED: Player+0x2220 is the CHECKPOINT SHADOW of char_save[16], not a crystals[8] array, and the header's crystals[8] / gargoyle_items[3] / legend_items[2] declarations at 0x2220-0x2239 are WRONG -- they are Xbox P_SAVE_STUFF field names misfiled onto Player, and live GC code actively writes a completion record inside the bytes the header labels gargoyle_items[2]. THE SHADOW ITSELF. Player carries a byte-for-byte 0x1434 snapshot of its persistent block: game/game/gamemain.c:3798 does *(PlayerSaveBlk*)(p + 7884) = *(PlayerSaveBlk*)(p + 2688) (PlayerSaveBlk = s32 w[1293] = 5172 = 0x1434) for each player with state == 1 when sMusicTrackHi == 13, i.e. on level entry; game/ui/select.c:1273 performs the identical assignment, and notably spells its SOURCE as offsetof(Player, name), pinning the live block's start at 0xA80; game/game/player.c:3473-3474 clears both blocks with the same size, memset(p + 0xA80, 0, 0x1434) and memset(p + 0x1ECC, 0, 0x1434). So [0x1ECC, 0x3300) mirrors [0xA80, 0x1EB4) with delta 0x1ECC - 0xA80 = 0x144C, and the mapping is arithmetically exact end to end: name[8] + pad_0A88[0x34C] = 0x354 bytes maps onto pad_1ECC[0x354] EXACTLY; char_save@0xDD4 maps to 0xDD4 + 0x144C = 0x2220 EXACTLY; char_save's end 0x1CD4 maps to 0x3120; and the live block's end 0x1EB4 maps to 0x3300, leaving 0x3300..0x3323 as the only genuinely non-shadow bytes before level@0x3324. THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE is not the arithmetic but three independent live consumers that all address the region with the char_save stride of 240 == 0xF0 == sizeof(PlayerCharSave), which is meaningless for a flat s16 counter array and inevitable for a char_save shadow. (1) game/world/tower.c:1289-1295 writes the LIVE slot through COMPLETION1_OFF (a macro defined at tower.c:248 as offsetof(Player, char_save) + offsetof(PlayerCharSave, completion1) = 0xDE8) and then, as the IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT statement, writes the literal displacement 8756 = 0x2234 -- same p->character * 240 stride, same j * 2 per-level index, same -1 value -- and 0x2234 - 0xDE8 = 0x144C exactly. (2) tower.c:1327-1333 repeats the identical paired live/shadow write for completion2: COMPLETION2_OFF = 0xDEE and literal 8762 = 0x223A, and 0x223A - 0xDEE = 0x144C exactly. These two pairs are the ground truth: the game deliberately clears a completion record in BOTH the live slot and its checkpoint so a later rollback cannot resurrect it. (3) game/shop/shop.c:1008 computes goldRaw = pl->gold - *(s32*)((b240 = pl + cls * 240) + offsetof(Player, field_224C)) with cls = pl->character, i.e. gold earned THIS LEVEL = current gold minus the level-entry snapshot; 0x224C - 0x144C = 0xE00 = char_save + 0x2C, and Xbox P_SAVE_STUFF carries an int gold at 0x30 -- the same role at the compaction-shifted offset. The header already called field_224C a 'per-character(*240) gold checkpoint' without knowing WHY it had a 240 stride; the shadow is the why. WHY THE EXISTING NAMES ARE WRONG. crystals[8], gargoyle_items[3] and legend_items[2] have ZERO consumers anywhere in the tree -- a name-level grep finds them only in the header itself -- so they are unverified documentation, never once referenced by code. Their source is research/xbox_symbols/misc.h:28884 struct P_SAVE_STUFF, which the header's own PlayerCharSave comment already identifies as the Xbox analogue of PLAYERCHARSAVE, NOT of Player: P_SAVE_STUFF holds legend_items@0x8, garg_items[3]@0x18 and crystals[8]@0x1e. These are therefore save-SLOT field names, and the only save slot that can exist at 0x2220 is the shadow of char_save[0]. Their claimed GC order (crystals, then gargoyle, then legend) does not even match P_SAVE_STUFF's order (legend, then garg, then crystals), so the placement was a guess rather than a derived mapping. Under the proven shadow mapping the bytes are instead: 0x2220..0x222F = shadow of rune_stones/rune_stones2/rune_near/pad_06/level_masks[0..3]; 0x2230/0x2232 = shadow of the boss_attempt1/boss_attempt2 pair this same run added at PlayerCharSave 0x10/0x12; 0x2234 = shadow of completion1, which tower.c:1295 provably writes and which the header currently mislabels gargoyle_items[2]; 0x223A = shadow of completion2, which tower.c:1333 provably writes and which the header currently leaves in pad_223A. CONSEQUENCES FOR THE NEXT PASS. The correct shape for [0x1ECC, 0x3300) is a mirror of [0xA80, 0x1EB4): char name_ckpt[8] @0x1ECC, a 0x34C pad, PlayerCharSave char_save_ckpt[16] @0x2220 running to 0x3120, then a 0x1E0 pad, then 0x24 real bytes to level@0x3324. Adopting it would let tower.c's two literal shadow writes and shop.c's field_224C all be spelled offsetof(Player, char_save_ckpt) + offsetof(PlayerCharSave, X) -- the same two-term house form tower.c already uses for the live side -- and would delete three wrong names. CRITICAL WARNING for whoever attempts it: PlayerCharSave char_save_ckpt[16] is an ARRAY-OF-STRUCT member, which is exactly the class that claim.law.embedded-struct-member-whole-tu-cascade.20260831.v1 proved can regress unrelated functions across an entire including TU (6 shop.c functions, none of which referenced the new field). That law's isolation protocol is MANDATORY there: gate the whole includer set after the header edit alone, before any site conversion. By contrast the scalar-only splits this run performed (7 scalar fields across Player and PlayerCharSave) gated clean on all five heavy includers, independently confirming the law's scalar-vs-aggregate boundary. A cheaper interim option that avoids the aggregate entirely is to correct only the three provably-wrong scalar names at 0x2220/0x2230/0x2236 and leave the array unmodelled.
